about: Prerequisite map for P5 Forces (brief docs/briefs/2026-11-27-phase-c-physics.md, Phase C B1, 2026-11-28): every idea the eight scripted lessons use, what each depends on (maths included), and where it is taught. Lessons run in syllabus order: p5-forces-motion, p5-newtons-laws, p5-stopping-distance, p5-momentum, p5-gravity, p5-elasticity, p5-moments, p5-fluid-pressure. P1 to P4 come first, so energy stores, kinetic energy, work done, elastic potential energy, density, particles and gas pressure may be recalled. Weight and W = mg are taught first in p5-newtons-laws key point 3 and again in p5-gravity key point 0, so p5-gravity recalls them. Used when scripting: each script teaches or recalls an idea before it asks about it.

ideas.name: A force is a push or a pull; measured in newtons (N)
ideas.taught: KS3 science; p5-forces-motion key point 5 (recalled at the start)

ideas.name: Energy stores, kinetic energy Ek = ½mv², work done W = Fs, elastic potential energy
Density ρ = m/V
Gas particles hit surfaces and push on them; that push spread over an area is pressure
Rearranging a three-term equation; units and converting cm to m, km to m, g to kg
Gradient of a straight line; area of a rectangle and triangle under a graph; a tangent to a curve
Squaring and square roots; direct proportion and the square law
Scalars have size only; vectors have size and direction
Distance along the path versus displacement from the start, with a direction
Speed = distance ÷ time; velocity is speed in a given direction; typical speeds
Gradient of a distance-time graph is speed
Acceleration a = Δv/t; deceleration; gradient of a velocity-time graph; area under it is distance
v² − u² = 2as for uniform acceleration
Contact forces (friction, air resistance, tension, normal contact force) and non-contact forces (gravity, magnetic, electrostatic)
Free fall near Earth at about 9.8 m/s²; terminal velocity when air resistance equals weight
ideas.taught: p5-forces-motion key point 4 (resultant force named here, taught in p5-newtons-laws key point 0)

ideas.name: Resultant force: the single force with the same effect as all the forces acting
Zero resultant force: at rest stays at rest, moving keeps a constant velocity; inertia
F = ma; inertial mass
Two objects interacting push on each other with equal and opposite forces
Weight W = mg (N); mass in kg; gravitational field strength g; centre of mass
ideas.taught: p5-newtons-laws key point 3; again in p5-gravity key point 0

ideas.name: Stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance
Reaction time (0.2 s to 0.9 s); tiredness, drugs, alcohol, distractions make it longer
Wet or icy roads, worn tyres, worn brakes; speed squared for a given braking force
The braking force does work: kinetic energy to thermal energy in the brakes; large decelerations are dangerous
Momentum p = mv (kg m/s), a vector
In a closed system, total momentum before = total momentum after
F = Δp/t: a longer stopping time means a smaller force (crumple zones, airbags, helmets)
A gravitational field is a region where a mass feels a force; it gets weaker further away
An orbit is continuous free fall; gravity provides the centripetal force; speed changes means the radius changes
Changing shape needs more than one force; elastic versus inelastic deformation
F = ke up to the limit of proportionality; extension; spring constant
Force–extension graph; linear and non-linear; gradient = k
Work done stretching a spring = elastic potential energy, Ee = ½ke²
Moment M = Fd, d the perpendicular distance from the pivot
Balanced: total clockwise moment = total anticlockwise moment
Levers and gears pass on the turning effect of a force
p = F/A in pascals; in a fluid the force acts at right angles to any surface
Pressure in a liquid grows with depth and density: p = hρg
Upthrust comes from more pressure underneath; floats if upthrust equals weight
The atmosphere is a thin layer of air; its pressure falls with height
